transcript:
User: Hello? Yeah... I got your card. You help with phones, right?
Agent: Hey, yeah, we do. Got your card—so you help with phones, right—makes sense.  

What caught your eye about that on the card?
User: Uh, I just need help... too many calls go to voicemail. Not sure how many, maybe ten? Fifteen?
Agent: Got it, so a bunch of those calls are just hitting voicemail... yeah, that adds up.  

When a call comes in and you’re out working or with a customer, who’s actually picking it up right now—anyone, or is it just going to voicemail?
User: Um, not really anyone. Mostly just goes to voicemail if I'm busy or out on a job.
Agent: Mhm, I hear you—that’s exactly the situation a lot of folks call us about.  

Those calls that go to voicemail now… do people usually leave a message, or do they just hang up and call the next guy?
User: Uh, some leave messages, but I think a lot just hang up and maybe call someone else.
Agent: Yeah… that’s the tough part, when they just move on to the next company.  

Roughly how many calls a week would you say are hitting voicemail instead of a real person—just a ballpark?
User: Uh, I don't know, maybe ten? Or fifteen a week? It's just a guess.
Agent: Yeah, that still adds up—10–15 chances a week is a lot.  

So with all that in mind, are you mainly looking for a way to make sure those calls get answered and turned into jobs even when you’re out on a job yourself?
User: Yeah, I need a way to answer calls when I'm busy. I miss a lot of chances for jobs.
Agent: Makes total sense—and you’re right, those are real chances for jobs slipping by.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what missing those 10–15 calls a week is actually costing you in dollars?
User: Uh, no, not really. I just know it can't be good for business.
Agent: Yeah, totally—if those calls are turning into jobs, it’s definitely not good for business.  

Mind if we do a super quick back-of-the-napkin math on it—like 30 seconds—to see what you’re actually leaving on the table?
User: Uh, sure, I guess. I don't really know the numbers, but we can try if you think it'll help.
Agent: Got it, yeah, we’ll keep it simple and just use your best guesses.  

So ballpark—out of those 10–15 calls a week that hit voicemail, how many would you say could’ve turned into actual jobs if someone answered?
User: Uh, I have no idea — maybe half? Or more? It's just hard to say for sure.
Agent: Got it, let’s go with “about half” for now—that’s totally fine for this.  

Next piece: when one of those calls *does* turn into a job, what’s a typical job worth for you—are we talking more like $200, $500, $1,000?
User: Uh, it depends on the job, maybe four hundred? Or five hundred? It's hard to say.
Agent: Perfect, let’s go with about $450 as a typical job.  

So with roughly 12 missed calls a week and half of those turning into $450 jobs, that’s about $2,700 a week… and around $11,600 a month walking away. Does that feel about right for your business?
User: Uh, yeah, I guess that sounds about right. Hard to tell, but losing business for sure.
Agent: Yeah… either way, we can agree it’s real money walking away every month.  

So, it’s a 20‑minute walkthrough where we show you exactly how to stop those missed calls from turning into lost jobs—what’s better for you for that, later today or tomorrow?
User: Uh, I think tomorrow might be better. What time are you thinking?
Agent: Makes sense, tomorrow works.  

So first step, I just need to grab a couple details for the schedule—what’s your first name?
User: Uh, it's Pedro. Just let me know what you need. I'm not the best with details, though.
Agent: Got it, Pedro, thanks for sticking with me on this.  

Next thing—what’s your last name?
User: Uh, it's Garcia. But I'm not great with details, so just bear with me, okay?
Agent: Totally fine, Pedro, you’re doing great—I’ll keep it simple.  

What’s the name of your company?
User: Uh, it's just Pedro's Landscaping. Not a big operation, just me and some help sometimes.
Agent: Got it, Pedro’s Landscaping—thanks, that helps.  

And… is the number you’re calling from right now the best number to reach you, or do you use a different one for business?
User: Uh, yeah, this number's fine. It's the one I use for everything, business too.
Agent: Perfect, that makes it easy.  

Since this is your main line, what’s the actual phone number, just so I can have it on file for the appointment and text confirmation?
User: Uh, it's 555-0123. That's the number I use for everything, so you can reach me there.
Agent: Got it, thanks—just one thing, I’ll need the full 10‑digit number so we can text you the confirmation.  

Can you read it for me slowly, with the area code first?
User: Uh, okay. It's 555-123-4567. Hope that's clear enough for you.
Agent: Mhm, that’s perfect, thanks for reading it out.  

Quick check—you’re on Mountain time there, right?
User: Uh, no, I think I'm in Central time. I'm not really sure, though.
Agent: Gotcha, Central time, that helps.  

For tomorrow, I can get you in Wednesday at either 7:00 in the evening or, if you prefer daytime, we can look at Thursday late morning—would tomorrow evening at 7 work for you?
User: Uh, tomorrow evening at 7 works for me. Let's go with that, I guess.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Pedro, the calendar’s giving us trouble locking it in right now because of the way your number is formatting on their side, but we’ve got your 7pm Central time noted, and we’ll give you a call at your number within the hour to firm up tomorrow’s 7 o’clock. Thanks for hanging in there with me today—and before I let you go, is there anything else about the missed calls you want us to be ready to look at with you tomorrow?
